chunks: And by this chain — from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Maryam — he said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say about a man who performs wudu, then calls his slave girl and she takes him by the hand until he reaches the mosque? For those among us claim that this constitutes al-mulamasah (the invalidating touch).'
He said: 'No, by Allah! There is no harm in that. Indeed, I myself have done so. And what is meant by this —'
— is nothing but sexual intercourse (muwaqaʿah) short of full penetration.'

key_terms.الْفَرْجِ: al-farj: the private parts; here denoting full penetration/complete intercourse
key_terms.الْمُلَامَسَةُ: al-mulamasah: physical touching/contact, debated here as a potential invalidator of wudu
key_terms.الْمُوَاقَعَةَ: al-muwaqaʿah: sexual congress/intercourse (specifically short of full penetration, as defined by the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Does a slave girl holding a man's hand to guide him to the mosque invalidate his wudu, according to Imam al-Baqir (AS)?
ai.summary: Abu Maryam asks Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) whether wudu is invalidated when a slave girl holds a man's hand to guide him to the mosque — a practice some contemporaries classified as al-mulamasah (the invalidating touch). The Imam firmly rules there is no harm in it, noting he himself has done so, and clarifies that the Quranic phrase 'or you have touched women' (4:43/5:6) refers exclusively to sexual congress (muwaqaʿah) falling short of full penetration, not mere physical contact.
